mainTopic: Justice and kindness in ה׳'s judgment, the י״ג מדות, and when תשובה can tear up a גזר דין (יחיד vs. ציבור)
overview: This amud opens with the end of a דרשה: ה׳ forgives the humble person who sees himself as a leftover. Then רב הונא, רבי אלעזר and אילפי each point to a פסוק that calls ה׳ both strictly just and very kind. They all answer the same way: strict justice at the time of judgment, kindness when the sentence is carried out. Next, רבי יוחנן explains that ה׳ showed משה the י״ג מדות as a prayer for forgiveness, and רב יהודה adds that a ברית guarantees they are never said in vain. רבי יוחנן then teaches that תשובה can tear up a גזר דין even after it is issued. A ברייתא seems to say that forgiveness comes only between ראש השנה and יום כיפור. The גמרא answers that a יחיד must repent before the seal, but a ציבור can have its decree torn up even later. It defends this rule against challenges from the rain ברייתא and the psalm of the sailors. Finally, it brings בלוריא הגיורת's question about two verses on ה׳ showing favor, and רבי יוסי הכהן's parable answering it. רבי עקיבא's different answer begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Forgiveness is for the person who sees himself as a leftover
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a דרשה on 'לשארית נחלתו‎.' ה׳ forgives the person who regards himself as שירים, a leftover of little importance.
steps.simpleTranslation: [ה׳ forgives sins] for one who makes himself like leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started earlier. It explains who 'שארית' (the remnant) in the פסוק refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ forgives sin 'לשארית נחלתו,' for the remnant of His inheritance. The גמרא reads 'שארית' as 'שירים,' leftovers. So forgiveness goes to someone who acts humble and does not make himself the center of everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftovers, remains: something of secondary importance
Remnant (the word in the פסוק being explained)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the ending of a דרשה on מיכה 7:18 that began earlier. It answers the question 'for whom does ה׳ forgive?'
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties forgiveness to humility, continuing the theme that a person who lets things go (מעביר על מדותיו) is forgiven.

phrases.english: For one who makes himself like leftovers.
phrases.notes: Plays on לשארית (remnant) → שירים (leftovers).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the דרשה on מיכה 7:18 earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ forgives sins for the humble person who regards himself as a leftover.

steps.title: רב הונא's contradiction: righteous or kind?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא points out that one פסוק calls ה׳ both צדיק (strictly just) and חסיד (going beyond the law).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא raised a contradiction: It is written, 'ה׳ is righteous in all His ways,' and it is written, 'and kind in all His works'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows two halves of a פסוק in תהלים (145:17) that seem to clash. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צדיק means acting by exact justice. חסיד means acting with kindness beyond what the law requires. These seem to be opposites, so how can both describe ה׳ at once?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (literally 'he threw' two sources against each other)
It is written ... and it is written: the formula for setting two verses side by side
Kind, acting beyond the letter of the law

phrases.english: Rav Huna raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'ה׳ is righteous in all His ways,'
phrases.notes: Psalms 145:17

phrases.english: and it is written: 'and kind in all His works'!
phrases.notes: The second half of the same verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on how justice and kindness fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Strict justice (צדיק) and going beyond the law (חסיד) seem to exclude each other.

steps.title: Answer: first righteous, then kind
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא resolves it by time: at first ה׳ is צדיק, and in the end He is חסיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning, righteous; and at the end, kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his own question. Both descriptions are true, but at different stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the time of judgment ה׳ judges by exact justice. When it comes time to carry out the punishment, He acts with kindness and softens it. So the two words describe two stages, not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning (at the time of judgment)
In the end (at the time of carrying out the sentence)
Beyond the letter of the law

phrases.english: At the beginning: righteous,
and at the end: kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating by time: two stages of one process
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צדיק and חסיד describe opposing behaviors at the same moment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strict justice at judgment, kindness when the sentence is carried out.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's contradiction: kindness or exact payment?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר notes that a פסוק says kindness belongs to ה׳, yet the same פסוק says He pays each person exactly by his deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר raised a contradiction: It is written, 'And to You, ה׳, belongs kindness,' and it is written, 'for You repay a man according to his deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר raises a second, similar contradiction from תהלים (62:13). His answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולך ה׳ חסד' suggests ה׳ goes beyond strict justice. 'תשלם לאיש כמעשהו' suggests exact measure for measure. Again, kindness and exact payment seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his deeds: exact measure

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'And to You, ה׳, belongs kindness,'
phrases.notes: Psalms 62:13

phrases.english: and it is written: 'for You repay a man according to his deeds.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel contradiction to רב הונא's, from a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Kindness beyond the law seems to contradict exact repayment for each deed.

steps.title: Answer: first exact payment, then kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers like רב הונא: at first ה׳ judges by deeds, and in the end He shows kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning: 'for You repay according to his deeds'; and at the end: 'and to You, ה׳, belongs kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר resolves his contradiction with the same 'first, then' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that he flips the order of the פסוק. The second half (exact payment) is the first stage, the judgment. The first half (kindness) is the final stage, when the punishment is carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: The time punishment is carried out

steps.confusionAlert: The answer reverses the order of the verse: the half that comes second in the פסוק ('כי אתה תשלם') is applied to the beginning stage.

phrases.english: At the beginning: 'for You repay according to his deeds,'
and at the end: 'and to You, ה׳, belongs kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 4 using the same model as step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating by time: judgment vs. execution
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Kindness and exact payment cannot both describe ה׳.
steps.terutzMaskana: Exact payment at judgment, kindness at the end.

steps.title: אילפי's contradiction: abundant kindness or truth?
steps.stepSummary: אילפי (or אילפא) notes that among the י״ג מדות ה׳ is called 'רב חסד' and also 'אמת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפי, and some say אילפא, raised a contradiction: It is written, 'and abundant in kindness,' and it is written, 'and truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא raises the same type of contradiction, this time from the י״ג מדות הרחמים in שמות (34:6). His answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'רב חסד' means ה׳ is full of kindness. 'אמת' means strict truth, which is justice. The question is again how both can be true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a different version of who said it
Two versions of the name of the same אמורא

phrases.english: Ilfai, and some say Ilfa, raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'and abundant in kindness,'
phrases.notes: Exodus 34:6

phrases.english: and it is written: 'and truth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel contradiction, this time from the תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Abundant kindness seems to contradict strict truth and justice.

steps.title: Answer: first truth, then abundant kindness
steps.stepSummary: אילפי answers: at first ה׳ judges with אמת, and in the end He acts with רב חסד.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the beginning: 'and truth'; and at the end: 'and abundant in kindness.'
steps.whatsHappening: אילפי resolves the contradiction with the same two-stage pattern as the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ first judges with strict truth. Then, since the world cannot survive on strict justice alone, He acts with abundant kindness. Again, the order of the פסוק is flipped to fit the stages.
steps.whatToRemember: Three אמוראים, three פסוקים, one idea: ה׳ begins with strict justice (צדיק, כמעשהו, אמת) at the time of judgment, and ends with kindness (חסיד, חסד, רב חסד) when the sentence is carried out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how ה׳ can be both a true judge and merciful, a central theme for ראש השנה, the day of judgment.

phrases.english: At the beginning: 'and truth,'
and at the end: 'and abundant in kindness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 6 and completes the series of three parallel contradictions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating by time: judgment vs. final outcome
steps.terutzMaskana: Truth at judgment, abundant kindness at the end.

steps.title: ה׳ teaches משה the order of prayer for forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads ״וַיַּעֲבוֹר ה׳ עַל פָּנָיו וַיִּקְרָא״ as ה׳ wrapping Himself like a שליח ציבור and showing משה the order of prayer that brings forgiveness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And ה׳ passed before him and called out.' רבי יוחנן said: If the פסוק had not written it, we could never say such a thing. It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא wrapped Himself like a שליח ציבור and showed משה the order of prayer. He told him: Whenever ישראל sin, let them do this order before Me, and I will forgive them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that opens the י״ג מדות, and רבי יוחנן explains what it means. ה׳ Himself 'acts out' the role of a שליח ציבור to teach משה how to pray for forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps quoted 'רב חסד' and 'אמת' from the י״ג מדות, so the גמרא now goes to the source of these מדות. רבי יוחנן says the picture is so bold that we could not say it without the פסוק. The point is practical: saying the י״ג מדות in this order is a set formula for winning forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: If the פסוק were not written (explicitly)
It would be impossible to say it
The leader of the communal prayer
The order or structure of the prayer

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take the picture literally, as if ה׳ has a body. 'אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב' signals that this is a bold image which the פסוק itself allows us to use, in order to teach a lesson about prayer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for saying the י״ג מדות in סליחות and on יום כיפור, led by the שליח ציבור.

phrases.english: "And ה׳ passed by before him and called out."
phrases.notes: שמות ל״ד:ו, the opening of the י״ג מדות

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Were it not that the verse is written,
it would be impossible to say it.
phrases.notes: It would seem disrespectful to ה׳'s honor.

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּתְעַטֵּף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כִּשְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, wrapped Himself like a prayer leader,
phrases.notes: 'Passed before him' is read as passing before the תיבה, like a חזן.

phrases.english: and showed Moshe the order of prayer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִין —
phrases.english: He said to him: Whenever Israel sins,
let them act before Me according to this order,
and I will forgive them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 6-7 quoted 'רב חסד' and 'אמת' from the י״ג מדות. The גמרא now goes to the פסוק that introduces those מדות and explains its deeper meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The י״ג מדות are a סדר תפילה given by ה׳. When ישראל recite them in this order after sinning, ה׳ forgives.

steps.title: Explaining the double name ״ה׳ ה׳״
steps.stepSummary: The repeated name ״ה׳ ה׳״ means ה׳ is the same merciful God before a person sins and after he sins and does תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ה׳ ה׳' means: I am the same One before a person sins, and I am the same One after a person sins and does תשובה, because I am 'a God merciful and gracious.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and explains why ה׳'s name appears twice. Each mention stands for a different time in a person's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name ה׳ stands for the מדת הרחמים. Saying it twice teaches that a person's sin does not change ה׳'s mercy toward him once he does תשובה‎. ה׳ treats him with the same רחמים as before he sinned, as the פסוק goes on to say: 'אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן.'

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳‎, ה׳: the double name opening the י״ג מדות

steps.confusionAlert: The second ה׳ does not mean ה׳ simply ignores sin. It applies to someone who sinned AND did תשובה ('וְיַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה').

phrases.aramaic: ״ה׳ ה׳״ — אֲנִי הוּא קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחְטָא הָאָדָם,
phrases.english: "ה׳‎, ה׳": I am He before a person sins,
phrases.notes: The first ה׳ stands for before the sin.

phrases.english: and I am He after a person sins
phrases.notes: The second ה׳ stands for after the sin.

phrases.english: and does repentance: "God, merciful and gracious."
phrases.notes: The continuation of the פסוק explains why: ה׳ is always merciful.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״ה׳ ה׳״ — אֲנִי הוּא קוֹדֶם שֶׁיֶּחְטָא הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק of the י״ג מדות, moving from 'ויעבור' to the words 'ה׳ ה׳'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s mercy toward a person stays the same after he sins and does תשובה as it was before he sinned.

steps.title: A ברית guarantees the י״ג מדות are answered
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that a ברית was made with the י״ג מדות so that they never return empty, based on ״הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי כּוֹרֵת בְּרִית״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A covenant was made with the thirteen attributes that they never come back empty, as it says: 'Behold, I make a covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds a guarantee to רבי יוחנן's teaching. Praying with the י״ג מדות always accomplishes something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said ה׳ will forgive when this order is followed. רב יהודה strengthens this into a binding ברית, learned from a פסוק a few verses later in the same פרשה (שמות ל״ד:י). 'אֵינָן חוֹזְרוֹת רֵיקָם' means one who calls out with them is sure to be answered in some way.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces the source פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברית is the reason the י״ג מדות are the centerpiece of סליחות and of נעילה on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A covenant was made with the thirteen attributes
that they will not return empty-handed,
phrases.notes: Whoever calls out with them will be answered.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Behold, I make a covenant."
phrases.notes: שמות ל״ד:י, right after the י״ג מדות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּרִית כְּרוּתָה לִשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's 'ואני מוחל להם' (step 8) by adding that the effectiveness of the י״ג מדות is sealed by a ברית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The י״ג מדות are guaranteed by ברית never to go unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: The י״ג מדות are a prayer formula ה׳ Himself taught (רבי יוחנן). They express that ה׳ stays merciful even after sin once there is תשובה (״ה׳ ה׳״). A ברית guarantees they are never said in vain (רב יהודה).

steps.title: תשובה tears up a person's decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that תשובה is great because it tears up a person's גזר דין, proven from ישעיה ו:י, 'וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Great is תשובה, for it tears up the decree against a person. As it says: 'Make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy, and seal their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and return and be healed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about the power of תשובה. He brings a פסוק from ישעיה as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק‎, ה׳ tells ישעיה to dull the people's senses so they will not do תשובה, meaning a punishment had already been decreed. Yet the פסוק itself admits that if they did return, 'וְרָפָא לוֹ', they would be healed. So תשובה is strong enough to cancel even a decree that was already issued.

keyTerms.meaning: A sentence or decree of judgment
And he will return and be healed

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not the first half of the פסוק, which describes sealing their senses. It is the ending: 'פֶּן... וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ‎.' ה׳ had to prevent their תשובה precisely because תשובה would have overturned the decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next discussion about whether תשובה helps before or after a גזר דין. It is also a foundational source for the idea in ונתנה תוקף that תשובה removes a harsh decree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Great is repentance, for it tears up a person's sentence,
as it is stated: "Make the heart of this people fat,"
phrases.notes: ישעיה ו:י. 'Fat' means dull or insensitive.

phrases.english: and make their ears heavy, and smear over their eyes;
lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears,
and understand with their heart, and return, and be healed."
phrases.notes: This ending is the proof: if they return, they are healed even though a decree was issued.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמְּקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theme of the י״ג מדות to a new, related teaching on the power of תשובה, echoing step 9's mention of 'וְיַעֲשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה can tear up a גזר דין already issued against a person, as shown by 'וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לוֹ'.

steps.title: Maybe תשובה only helps before the decree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי whether רבי יוחנן's teaching only covers תשובה done before the גזר דין is issued.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But maybe the verse is talking about before the sentence was issued?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's claim that תשובה 'tears up' a גזר דין. Maybe it only works before the sentence is actually given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said תשובה can cancel a sentence. רב פפא suggests a smaller reading: the verse may only mean that תשובה prevents a bad sentence from being issued. If so, there is no proof that תשובה cancels a sentence that already exists.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a possible alternative reading)
An אמורא, student of אביי and רבא

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But perhaps it refers to before the sentence was issued?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְדִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רבי יוחנן's proof from ישעיה reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that תשובה tears up an existing גזר דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse could describe תשובה before judgment, so it does not prove that a sentence already issued can be cancelled.

steps.title: Healing means there was already a sickness
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the word 'וְרָפָא' (healing) shows there is already something bad in place, which is the גזר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It is written 'and be healed.' What needs healing? You must say: a sentence that was already decreed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יוחנן by looking closely at one word in the verse. 'Healing' only makes sense if something bad has already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only heal someone who is already sick. So the verse describes a person who already has a sentence against him, and תשובה heals him from it. This proves that תשובה works even after the גזר דין is issued.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will be healed (ישעיה ו:י)
Healing, which assumes there is already an illness
You must therefore say (introduces the only possible conclusion)

phrases.english: He said to him:
"And be healed" is written.
What is a thing that needs healing?
You must say: this is a sentence that was already issued.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse might only mean that תשובה prevents a bad sentence.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Healing' assumes an existing illness, so תשובה cancels a sentence even after it is decreed.

steps.title: A ברייתא says repentance only helps between ראש השנה and יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: if a person repents in between, he is forgiven. If not, even the finest offerings will not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who repents in the meantime is forgiven. One who did not repent in the meantime is not forgiven, even if he brings all the אילי נביות in the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי and רבי יוחנן from a ברייתא. It seems to say that once the decree is sealed, nothing can change it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the meantime' means between ראש השנה, when judgment begins, and יום כיפור, when it is sealed. The ברייתא says that if a person missed this window, even the best קרבנות will not help. That sounds like תשובה cannot tear up a sentence once it is final, which contradicts what was just proven.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
In the meantime, between ראש השנה and יום כיפור
The rams of Nebaioth, the finest rams, used here for the best possible offerings

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who repents in the meantime
is forgiven.
If he did not repent in the meantime,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֵבִיא כׇּל אֵילֵי נְבָיוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
phrases.english: even if he brought all the rams of Nebaioth in the world,
he is not forgiven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 13 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תשובה tears up a גזר דין even after it is issued.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits forgiveness to the period before the sentence is sealed. After that, nothing helps.

steps.title: Individual versus community
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא speaks about a יחיד, while רבי יוחנן's teaching speaks about a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is about an individual, and that one is about the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual must repent before יום כיפור, or his sentence stays. When the whole community repents, the sentence can be torn up even after it is decreed. The verse in ישעיה is about 'הָעָם הַזֶּה', the whole people, which fits a ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer that splits the cases)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is: an individual's sentence can be changed only until יום כיפור. The community's תשובה can tear up a sentence even after it is sealed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about an individual,
that one is about the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּיָחִיד הָא בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by type of penitent)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody's sentence can be changed after it is sealed.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a יחיד, תשובה must come before the seal. For a ציבור, תשובה tears up even a sealed decree.

steps.title: The rain ברייתא, part one: a decree that cannot be added to
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if ישראל was wicked on ראש השנה and later repented, ה׳ cannot add rain because the decree was issued. Instead, He makes the little rain fall at the right time and place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'The eyes of ה׳ your God are upon it.' Sometimes for good and sometimes for bad. How is it for good? Suppose ישראל was completely wicked on ראש השנה, and little rain was decreed for them. In the end they repented. Adding rain is impossible, because the decree was already issued. Instead, ה׳ brings the rain down at the right time, on land that needs it, all according to the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the answer that a community's תשובה can tear up a decree. Here the whole nation repented, yet the amount of rain could not be changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is about all of ישראל, which is a ציבור. They did תשובה after ראש השנה. Even so, the ברייתא says the decree could not be changed ('לְהוֹסִיף אִי אֶפְשָׁר‎'). ה׳ only improves how the rain is used, which seems to contradict the idea that a ציבור's תשובה tears up the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: The eyes of ה׳ your God are upon it (דברים יא:יב)
The decree has already been issued

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חָזְרוּ בָּהֶן' means they turned back to good, that is, they repented. In the next case the very same words mean the opposite.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "The eyes of the Lord your God are upon it"
sometimes for good, sometimes for bad.
Sometimes for good, how so?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: Suppose Israel were completely wicked on Rosh HaShana
and a small amount of rain was decreed for them,
and in the end they repented.
To add to them is impossible,
because the decree was already issued.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹרִידָן בִּזְמַנָּן,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings them down at their proper time,
on the land that needs them,
all according to the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the יחיד/ציבור split from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a ציבור's תשובה tears up a decree after it is issued.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All of ישראל repented, yet the decree could not be changed. Only the way it was carried out improved.

steps.title: The rain ברייתא, part two: a decree that cannot be reduced
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if ישראל was righteous on ראש השנה and later sinned, ה׳ cannot reduce the rain. Instead, He makes it fall at the wrong time and in the wrong place.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it for bad? Suppose ישראל was completely righteous on ראש השנה, and much rain was decreed for them. In the end they turned bad. Reducing the rain is impossible, because the decree was already issued. Instead, ה׳ brings the rain down at the wrong time, on land that does not need it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the mirror-image case. In the next step the גמרא spells out exactly what this ברייתא implies against רבי יוחנן, and then it answers in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This half shows the same rule from the other side: once the amount is decreed, it stays fixed. ה׳ only changes when and where the rain falls, so much rain becomes useless. Both halves together show that a sealed decree on the community is not cancelled, only redirected.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חָזְרוּ בָּהֶן' means they turned away from good and began to sin. It is not repentance, even though the same words meant repentance in step 16.

phrases.english: Sometimes for bad, how so?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: Suppose Israel were completely righteous on Rosh HaShana
and much rain was decreed for them,
and in the end they turned bad.
To reduce them is impossible,
because the decree was already issued.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹרִידָן שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּן,
phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings them down not at their proper time,
on land that does not need them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 16 as part of the same challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a ציבור's change of behavior alters a sealed decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mirror case confirms that the decreed amount is fixed and only how it is carried out changes. This reinforces the challenge from step 16.

steps.title: Why not tear up the decree and add rain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses on the rain ברייתא. When ישראל repents, why doesn't ה׳ just tear up the decree and give more rain?
steps.simpleTranslation: At least when it is for good, let Him tear up their decree and add rain for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן again using the rain ברייתא from Step 16. If a ציבור's decree can be torn up, ה׳ should simply add rain when they repent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that when ישראל repents, ה׳ 'cannot' add rain because the decree was already set. That sounds like even a whole ציבור cannot get its decree torn up, which goes against רבי יוחנן. The point of 'לטובה מיהא' is that tearing up the decree here would only bring good, so it should surely happen.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new source. The גמרא is still working with the same rain ברייתא from Steps 16-17 and pointing out what it seems to imply.

phrases.english: For good, at least,
phrases.notes: Refers to the case where ישראל repented, so the change would be for their benefit.

phrases.english: let Him tear up their decree
phrases.notes: Echoes רבי יוחנן's language, 'מְקָרַעַת גְּזַר דִּינוֹ' (step 11).

phrases.english: and add rain for them!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְטוֹבָה מִיהָא, לִיקְרְעֵיהּ לִגְזַר דִּינַיְיהוּ וְלוֹסֵיף לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the rain ברייתא (Steps 16-17) against the יחיד/ציבור distinction the גמרא made in Step 15 to defend רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule (as explained in Step 15) that a ציבור's גזר דין can be torn up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is about all of ישראל, a ציבור, and it says that even after they repent ה׳ does not add rain. That implies the decree cannot be torn up even for a ציבור.

steps.title: No need to tear up the decree when another way works
steps.stepSummary: The decree isn't torn up there only because the same good can be reached another way: perfect timing and placement of the rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is possible to help them in this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rain case is special. ה׳ can help the people without tearing up the decree, so He does not tear it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the small amount of rain at the right time and the right place already brings them full benefit. So the ברייתא does not prove that a ציבור's decree can never be torn up. It only shows that ה׳ does not tear it up when there is no need to.

keyTerms.meaning: because it is possible in this way

phrases.english: It is different there
because it is possible in this way.
phrases.notes: That is, by making the rain fall at the proper time and place (Step 16).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: an alternative solution makes tearing up the decree unnecessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that a ציבור's decree cannot be torn up at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ציבור's decree can be torn up. In the rain case ה׳ simply chooses a different way to help, so nothing is disproven.

steps.title: The psalm of the sailors in the storm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings verses from תהלים about sailors caught in a storm who cry out to ה׳. This sets up a new challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Those who go down to the sea in ships, who do work in great waters, they saw the works of ה׳... He spoke and raised a stormy wind, which lifted up its waves. They reel and stagger like a drunk man... They cried out to ה׳ in their trouble... Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge by quoting the psalm about sailors in a storm. This step is setting up the next move, where the גמרא will explain what these verses teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses describe a storm, the sailors crying out, and then their rescue and thanks. On its own this sounds like prayer always helps. The point of the challenge will come in the next step, from special markers written in these verses.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source used as proof or challenge)
those who go down to the sea (sailors)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Those who go down to the sea in ships
phrases.notes: תהלים 107:23

phrases.english: who do work in great waters.
they saw the works of ה׳, etc.
He spoke and raised a stormy wind
which lifted up its waves.
They reel and stagger like a drunk man, etc.

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּצְעֲקוּ אֶל ה׳ בַּצַּר לָהֶם וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: They cried out to ה׳ in their trouble, etc.
Let them thank ה׳ for His kindness, etc.
phrases.notes: תהלים 107:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 19 settled the rain ברייתא, this opens a fresh challenge against רבי יוחנן from a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that prayer can tear up a decree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The attack comes from how these verses are read in Step 21.

steps.title: Markers teach: crying out helps only before the decree
steps.stepSummary: Special markers in these verses work like limiting words. They teach that crying out helps before the decree but not after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse made markers for them, like the words 'אך' and 'רק' in the תורה, to tell you: if they cried out before the decree, they are answered. If they cried out after the decree, they are not answered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge. Special markers in the psalm limit the rescue to people who prayed before the decree, which seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words like אך and רק in the תורה narrow down a rule. These markers do the same thing here: the rescue in the psalm only applies when they cried out before the decree. So prayer after the decree does not help, which seems to go against רבי יוחנן's teaching that a decree can be torn up.

keyTerms.meaning: markers (inverted letter נ written in the psalm)
the limiting words 'אך' and 'רק' in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The markers are not words that are read aloud. They are scribal signs in the text, and the גמרא learns from them the way it learns from limiting words.

phrases.english: He made markers for them
phrases.notes: The inverted נ symbols placed by these verses.

phrases.english: like the 'but' and 'only' words in the Torah,
phrases.notes: These are words that limit or exclude.

phrases.english: to tell you:
if they cried out before the decree, they are answered;

phrases.aramaic: צָעֲקוּ לְאַחַר גְּזַר דִּין — אֵינָן נַעֲנִין!
phrases.english: if they cried out after the decree, they are not answered!

steps.triggerLanguage: עָשָׂה לָהֶן סִימָנִיּוֹת כְּאַכִּין וְרַקִּין שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in Step 20 by explaining what the verses teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a decree can be torn up through prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The markers limit the rescue to prayer before the decree. Prayer after the decree is not answered, so the decree is not torn up.

steps.title: Sailors count as individuals
steps.stepSummary: The sailors are treated like יחידים, so the rule that a decree cannot be torn up applies to them, not to a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: These too are considered like individuals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using the same distinction as Step 15. People on a ship are like יחידים, not a ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if there are many sailors, they are only a small group, not a whole community. So the psalm teaches that a יחיד's decree is not torn up after it is sealed. רבי יוחנן's rule about a ציבור stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: The line holds: a ציבור's גזר דין can be torn up by prayer and תשובה, while a יחיד's cannot once it is sealed. Each challenge is answered by showing that its case involves יחידים (the sailors) or did not need the decree torn up (the rain).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far the idea of 'ציבור' reaches. A group of many people is still not a ציבור unless it is the whole community, and that gives communal prayer its special power.

phrases.english: These too
are considered like individuals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Steps 20-21 by applying the יחיד/ציבור distinction from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case classification: the sailors fall into the יחיד category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The psalm seemed to show that no decree can be changed by prayer after it is sealed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The psalm is about יחידים, so it does not contradict רבי יוחנן's rule for a ציבור.

steps.title: A convert points out two verses that seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: With תא שמע, the גמרא brings a new source. בלוריא הגיורת asks רבן גמליאל how one verse can say ה׳ does not show favor while another says ה׳ will show favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בלוריא the convert asked רבן גמליאל: It is written in your תורה, 'who does not show favor,' and it is also written, 'ה׳ shall lift His face toward you (show you favor).' How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source. In it, a convert points out that two verses seem to say opposite things about ה׳ showing favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Verse one (דברים) says ה׳ 'does not show favor,' meaning He does not let anyone off. Verse two (ברכת כהנים in במדבר) says ה׳ 'will show favor' to you. The question is simple: does ה׳ show favor or not? The answers that follow will tie into the sugya's discussion of when a decree can be changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an opening for a source the גמרא is bringing into the discussion
He does not 'lift the face', meaning He does not show favor or let someone off
ה׳ shall lift His face to you, meaning He will show you favor (from ברכת כהנים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lifting the face' (נשיאת פנים) is an idiom. It means showing favor or giving a pass. It has nothing to do with a physical face.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answers to this contradiction will connect back to the sugya's main question: does crying out to ה׳ help after a decree has been sealed?

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלָה בְּלוֹרְיָא הַגִּיּוֹרֶת אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Beloreya the convert asked Rabban Gamliel:
It is written in your Torah: "who does not show favor"
phrases.notes: דברים י:יז

phrases.english: and it is written: "ה׳ shall show favor to you"?
phrases.notes: במדבר ו:כו, from ברכת כהנים

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שָׁאֲלָה בְּלוֹרְיָא הַגִּיּוֹרֶת אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer that the sailors count as יחידים, the גמרא brings another source that relates to whether a decree can be changed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 15 (defending רבי יוחנן) that a ציבור's תשובה can tear up a גזר דין even after it is issued. Inside the quoted story, בלוריא's own question targets how the two verses about ה׳ showing favor fit together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Within the story, one verse says ה׳ never shows favor and the other says He does. The גמרא brings this source because the resolution it leads to (רבי עקיבא's, starting in step 25) will suggest that after a גזר דין, ה׳ does not show favor, which challenges the rule that a decree can be torn up.

steps.title: The parable of the borrower and the king
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הכהן answers with a parable. A king forgives the insult to himself but sends the borrower to appease the lender. Likewise, ה׳ shows favor for sins against Him but not for sins against other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הכהן joined in and said to her: I will give you a parable. A man lent his friend a מנה (a sum of money) and set a due date in front of the king. The borrower swore by the king's life that he would pay. The date came and he did not pay. He went to appease the king, and the king said: 'I forgive the insult to me. Go appease your friend.' Here too: one verse ('ה׳ will show favor') is about sins between a person and ה׳, and the other ('does not show favor') is about sins between a person and his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הכהן resolves the contradiction with a story. Each verse is talking about a different kind of sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower wronged two parties. He insulted the king by breaking an oath on the king's life, and he hurt the lender by not paying. The king can only forgive his own insult, so the borrower must still make it right with the lender. In the same way, ה׳ 'shows favor' and forgives sins against Himself, but 'does not show favor' for sins against people until the victim is appeased.

keyTerms.meaning: Joined in with her (entered the conversation)
To appease, to make peace with someone you wronged
Between a person and his fellow

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הכהן's answer: ה׳ forgives sins against Himself ('will show favor'), but for sins against people, ה׳ does not let you off ('does not show favor') until you appease the person you hurt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This matches a well-known halacha (taught in the משנה in יומא): even on יום כיפור, sins against another person are not forgiven until you appease that person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei the Kohen joined in with her.
He said to her: I will give you a parable.
To what is the matter comparable?
To a person whose friend owed him a maneh
and he set him a due date in front of the king,
and the borrower swore to him by the life of the king.
The time came and he did not repay him.
He came to appease the king,
and the king said to him: The insult to me is forgiven;
go and appease your friend.
Here too:
here, it refers to sins between a person and ה׳;
phrases.notes: The verse 'ה׳ will show favor to you'

phrases.english: there, it refers to sins between a person and his fellow.
phrases.notes: The verse 'who does not show favor'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised by בלוריא הגיורת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each verse refers to a different kind of sin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses seem to describe ה׳ in opposite ways about the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Will show favor' refers to sins against ה׳, which He forgives. 'Does not show favor' refers to sins against people, which need the victim's forgiveness.

steps.title: Setting up רבי עקיבא's different answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוסי הכהן's answer stood until רבי עקיבא came and taught a different way to resolve the verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until רבי עקיבא came and taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to bring a different answer to the same contradiction, from רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'until רבי עקיבא came' signal that רבי יוסי הכהן's answer was the accepted one until a new approach appeared. The actual content of רבי עקיבא's teaching comes in the next part of the גמרא. That answer is the one that ties back to the sugya's topic of decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Until [he] came: signals that an earlier view held until a new teaching arrived

steps.confusionAlert: The teaching of רבי עקיבא is not in this line. It continues in the next section, so do not look for his answer here.

phrases.english: Until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second, different resolution to the same contradiction that רבי יוסי הכהן answered.
